svg.text: Centralized Lakehouse vs Domain-Owned Mesh — Decision Factors
When to keep one central team · when to federate into Fabric domains · signals that a mesh is premature
START — WEIGH THE SIGNALS

g.text: 1 · Number of autonomous producing teams
One team owns curation end to end?
Many departments each own & publish their own data?
Fabric hook: domains group each department's workspaces (delegated admin).
2 · Governance delegation need
Central team can set all policy centrally?
Departments need to override delegated settings themselves?
Fabric hook: tenant → domain → workspace three-tier settings hierarchy.
3 · Cost isolation & chargeback
One shared bill is acceptable?
Each domain must be billed & throttled independently?
Fabric hook: capacity = isolation + chargeback boundary; throttled per-capacity.
4 · Cross-team data sharing pattern
Reuse is occasional / within one lakehouse?
Teams routinely consume each other's published products?
Fabric hook: OneLake shortcuts share across domains zero-copy, no ETL.
5 · Trust / discovery signalling
Consumers already know where data lives?
Consumers need cataloged, certified, discoverable products?
Fabric hook: OneLake Catalog + Promoted/Certified endorsement.

svg.text: Lean CENTRALIZED lakehouse

g.text: ◂ 1 · A single team owns curation
◂ 2 · Policy set centrally, little delegation
◂ 3 · Shared bill / no chargeback demand
◂ 4 · Sharing stays within one lakehouse
◂ 5 · Small, known consumer set

svg.text: Realize as:
• One (or few) workspaces, one capacity
• Optionally one domain for grouping only
• Central team owns lakehouse + semantic models
• Mesh is PREMATURE here — extra domains and
capacities add overhead with no ownership to match.
Lean DOMAIN-OWNED mesh

g.text: ▸ 1 · Many teams own & publish independently
▸ 2 · Departments override delegated settings
▸ 3 · Per-domain billing & throttle isolation
▸ 4 · Heavy cross-team product consumption
▸ 5 · Broad consumer base needs a catalog

svg.text: Realize as:
• One domain per business area (subdomains ok)
• Producer + consumer workspaces per domain
• Own capacity per domain for cost + isolation
• Certified products shared via shortcuts
• Central plane keeps tenant policy + catalog
Signals a mesh is PREMATURE (inference)

g.text: • Only one team actually owns the data — federation invents boundaries no one staffs.
• Departments lack the skills to own pipelines, quality, and their own semantic models.
• No real chargeback requirement — splitting capacities just fragments burst headroom.
• Consumers are few and already know the data — a catalog + endorsement is overkill.
• Start centralized; carve out a domain only once a team genuinely owns a product.

svg.text: Either way, the central platform plane stays

g.text: • One tenant = one OneLake — the physical lake is shared regardless of how you draw domains.
• Tenant-level Purview governance, sensitivity labels, DLP, and compliance certs apply to all data landing in OneLake.
• Mesh federates OWNERSHIP and delegated policy — it does NOT create separate physical lakes (that is the OneLake anti-pattern).

svg.text: Fabric mechanics (domains, capacities, shortcuts, catalog, endorsement) are claim-grounded.
The centralized-vs-mesh weighing and "premature" signals are architectural inference.
Use the factors as a lean-left / lean-right guide, not a hard gate — most estates run a mix.
Fabric Atlas — original diagram, July 2026. Not a Microsoft asset.
